content.title: Eid ul Fitr 2026 LIVE as Muslims gather for prayers and celebrations
content.text: NewsUK NewsEidLIVE EVENT ENDEDLast updated 20th March 2026Muslims around the world marked the end of Ramadan today (March 20)People gather in Birmingham to perform Eid al-Fitr prayers on Friday(Image: Getty Images)Updated 21:16, 20 Mar 2026Muslims across the world are getting ready for Eid ul Fitr 2026, marking the end of Ramadan. Eid is commemorated with prayer, gift giving and sharing huge feasts with family and friends.Also known as the 'festival of breaking the fast' Eid-al-Fitr is the festival held once Ramadan is complete. After weeks of observing the holy month, millions across the globe will now find out when celebrations to mark the end of Ramadan will begin.Eid ul Fitr 2026 was announced as being on Friday, March 20, in Saudi Arabia after officials in the kingdom unsuccessfully attempted to sight the new crescent moon on Wednesday.The date of the holy fetsival is determined by the sighting of the crescent of a new moon. Muslims traditionally look for the crescent on day 29 of Ramadan.Ramadan ends when the crescent moon is seen - signal the beginning of the next month, Shawwal. Eid ul Fitr will take place on its first day and festivities can last for three days.20th Mar21:15 BSTEnd of coverageThat marks the end of our coverage of Eid this year. To the Muslim communities of Greater Manchester, we wish you Eid Mubarak.20th Mar21:14 BSTAll the best pictures from celebrations in Platt Fields Park Here's a roundup of all the best photos from this year's celebrations in Platt Fields Park: All the best pictures as hundreds celebrate Eid in Platt Fields Park20th Mar14:54 BSTGathering in HuddersfieldThe Ahmadiyya Muslim Association Huddersfield marked Eid-ul-Fitr at the Accu Stadium, where more than 700 members, including men, women, and children, gathered in a spirit of unity and celebration.The Ahmadiyya Muslim Association Huddersfield marked Eid-ul-Fitr at the Accu Stadium(Image: Manchester Evening News)20th Mar14:50 BSTFamilies coming togetherFamilies are spending the day celebrating, including plenty of great fun for the kids.Families together in Birmingham(Image: Getty Images)20th Mar14:38 BSTBirmingham celebrationsPeople gathering in Birmingham after prayers.People gather in Small Heath Park after performing Eid al-Fitr prayers and celebrate the end of Ramadan in Birmingham(Image: Getty Images)20th Mar14:28 BSTEid around the UKThere are some lovely images of people celebrating across the UK, including Birmingham.People enjoy a funfair ride after gathering in Small Heath Park to perform Eid al-Fitr prayers and celebrate the end of Ramadan in Birmingham(Image: Getty Images)20th Mar12:23 BSTCommunity events, fairs and public celebrationsCharity is another key part of Eid. Muslims are encouraged to give Zakat al-Fitr, a donation intended to help those in need take part in the festivities. Community events, fairs and public celebrations may also take place in towns and cities, making Eid both a religious and social occasion.20th Mar12:09 BSTTraffic disruption as celebrations get underwayQueueing traffic due to eid celebrations on A665 Cheetham Hill Road in both directions at Heath Street.20th Mar11:27 BSTFamily gatherings and festive mealsThe day is also centred around family gatherings and festive meals, with traditional dishes and sweets shared throughout the celebrations. Children may receive gifts or money, often known as “Eidi,” while many adults exchange presents or visit relatives they may not have seen during Ramadan.20th Mar11:26 BSTHow is Eid al-Fitr being celebrated this morning?Eid al-Fitr celebrations usually begin with special morning prayers held at mosques or large outdoor venues, where Muslims gather to mark the end of the fasting month of Ramadan. People often wear new or their best clothes for the occasion and spend time greeting friends, neighbours and members of the wider community.20th Mar11:10 BSTWhy is Eid al-Fitr today?Religious authorities and local moon-sighting groups observe the sky after sunset on the 29th day of Ramadan to determine whether the crescent is visible. If it is seen, Eid takes place the following day. If not, Ramadan continues for one more day before the festival is held.This tradition reflects the importance of the lunar Islamic calendar, which is based on the phases of the moon rather than fixed dates, meaning Eid al-Fitr falls on a different day each year in the Gregorian calendar.Cloudy conditions in Sudair made it impossible to see Shawwal crescent moon, meaning that Ramadan will complete 30 days, making Eid al Fitr on Friday, March 20.20th Mar11:06 BSTWhy is the moon important?The moon is significant for Eid al-Fitr because the festival begins when the new crescent moon is sighted, marking the end of the holy month of Ramadan. Muslims fast throughout Ramadan, and the appearance of the Shawwal crescent signals that the period of fasting has finished and celebrations can begin.20th Mar11:03 BSTWhat is Eid-al-Fitr?Also known as the 'festival of breaking the fast' Eid-al-Fitr is the festival held once Ramadan is complete. It is commemorated with prayer, gift giving and sharing huge feasts with family and friends.19th Mar21:26 BSTOutdoor Manchester Eid prayer cancelled this yearThe popular Eid prayer has been cancelled this year. The news comes Muslims across the region prepare to celebrate the end of Ramadan on Friday (March 20).Organisers say that the outdoor prayer, which is held at Platt Fields Park, Fallowfield, has been postponed due to "safety and operational requirements" relating to terrain and parking spaces.The event, which is known to attract more than 20,000 people since its inception in 2017, usually features prayers, food stalls, local traders, and a funfair.Read more here.19th Mar20:46 BSTNew Crescent Society announce negative sighting of moonBritish moon sighting group, New Crescent Society, say that there was no positive sighting of a new crescent moon from their volunteers across the UK.This means that worshippers following their advice will see out 30 days of the holy month and celebrate Eid on Saturday (March 21).The group do not except observaton carried out by specialist equipment and solely rely on sightings made by the naked eye.It is one of very few Islamic institutions in the UK who will be observing the festival on Saturday, most of the UK Muslim community will be gathering on Friday (March 20).19th Mar20:39 BSTPrime Minister wishes Muslim community Eid Mubarak Sir Keir Starmer has wished the Muslim community a happy Eid.Warmest wishes to Muslims who are marking the end of Ramadan across the UK and around the world.May your Eid‑al‑Fitr be joyful and full of peace.Eid Mubarak. https://t.co/YaTP2xK5ki— Keir Starmer (@Keir_Starmer) March 19, 2026 19th Mar20:37 BSTHow to wish someone Eid Mubarak If you are one of those who would like to extend your well wishes to the Muslim community or are curious about the etiquette around Eid celebrations, here is a quick guide.To wish someone a happy Eid, you can say "Eid Mubarak" , which means "have a blessed Eid". You can also say "Eid Saeed", meaning "Happy Eid".Eid-al-Fitr, is also marked with prayer, good deeds and donating to charity.19th Mar20:35 BSTRochdale mosque to host outdoor prayersThe Jalalia Jaame Mosque is hosting an outdoor prayer in Rochdale.Two prayers have been scheduled at 9am and 10.30am on Nile Street.19th Mar20:28 BSTManchester Central Mosque announces prayer timesThe Victoria Park mosque has revealed the prayer times for tomorrow's Eid celebrations.Five prayers are set to take place at 6.45am, 7.45, 8.45am, 9.45am and 10.45am.19th Mar19:37 BSTManchester Central Mosque announces Eid prayer The Manchester Central Mosque has confirmed to its congregration that Eid will take place on Friday (March 20).One of the largest mosques in Manchester, thousands of people will be expected at the venue.19th Mar19:20 BSTMorocco confirms Eid dateThe Kingdom of Morocco's Ministry of Endowments and Islamic Affairs has confirmed Eid Al Fitr will be celebrated on Friday (March 20).19th Mar18:49 BSTLive UK moon sighting The New Crescent Society is broadcasting live.19th Mar18:10 BSTSalford Council wishes residents Eid Mubarak Salford City Council has taken to social media to wish residents Eid Mubarak.19th Mar18:07 BSTFire services wishes Eid Mubarak The Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service has wished the Muslim community a happy Eid.Along with their message came some safety warning tips such as., never leave cooking unattended and keeping tea towels and cloths away from the hob.19th Mar17:44 BSTWhat time will local mosques announce Eid?While many masjids have confirmed their Eid prayers, some mosques opted to wait until this evening before making announcements.This is because they are either following the moon sightings in the UK or Morocco, rather than that of Saudi Arabia.The new crescent moon is expected to be spotted in around an hours’ time. Expect announcements from 6.30pm.19th Mar13:40 BSTPrayer times at Rochdale mosque announcedThese are the prayer times at Jamia Masjid Bilal in Rochdale. They'll be held either tomorrow or Saturday, subject to moonsighting.19th Mar13:22 BSTEid in the Park cancellation 'not due to anti-Muslim pressure'Fallowfield councillor Ali Ilyas has commented on the cancellation of the Platt Fields Park Eid prayer event. Writing on his Facebook page he said:On this occasion the Eid in the Park organisers and Manchester City Council jointly decided due to operational issues for the congregational prayer to not take place in Platt Fields park. This was not from any perceived or alleged Anti Muslim pressure.We need to resist anyone causing division in our city or spreading misinformation. We are a proud diverse city, and we’ll always champion that.19th Mar11:19 BSTMoon sighting meeting being held in Manchester this afternoonHere are the details of a moon sighting meeting being held at Anwaar ul Haramain Jamè Masjid in Cheetham Hill this afternoon.19th Mar09:26 BSTDetails of Dubai's Eid mass prayer announcedThe Dubai Media Office has confirmed the details for tomorrow's mass Eid Al Fitr prayer, held across 900 mosques in the UAE's largest city.The Eid Al Fitr prayer in Dubai will be held at 6:40am with full readiness ensured across more than 900 mosques, in coordination with the Dubai Resilience Centre. The ‘Muezzin Al Freej’ initiative will continue, with Eid Takbeerat raised and the call to prayer delivered across… pic.twitter.com/g7IE5dIX4K— Dubai Media Office (@DXBMediaOffice) March 19, 2026 19th Mar09:19 BSTRochdale Council of Mosques meeting tonightRochdale Council of Mosques is meeting tonight at the town's Golden Mosque. They say they will update their social media 'as soon as we have a verified report the Crescent moon of Shawwal has been sighted'.In a statement yesterday CEO Nadeem Mir explained how consensus over the sighting is reached. He wrote:This process has required cooperation, mutual respect, and flexibility from all involved, while remaining firmly grounded in the principles of our Deen. Achieving such unity has not been without its challenges; however, Alhamdulillah, a balanced and inclusive approach has been established, enabling many families to celebrate this blessed occasion of Eid together.In today’s fast-paced digital age, numerous announcements regarding the day of Eid may circulate throughout the day, particularly via social media. This can understandably lead to confusion and uncertainty within the community.Rochdale Council of Mosques will continue to follow its established and agreed procedure. This includes giving due consideration to verified local moon sightings, followed by the official process of The Kingdom Of Morocco, Ministry of Endowments and Islamic Affairs. Consideration will also be given to confirmed sightings from South Africa.It is important to note that when the moon is not sighted, announcements from the Rochdale Council of Mosques may be delayed. This is due to the comprehensive reporting process in Morocco, where over 278 observation sites must submit their negative findings before any official decision is announced by the Ministry. This thorough process ensures accuracy, but may result in a later communication.To keep the community informed and reassured, the Rochdale Council of Mosques will issue an initial statement, followed by timely updates as information becomes available. We kindly ask for your patience and understanding during this period, as trustees work diligently to uphold a unified and reliable approach for the benefit of all.
